name: Kitchen housewares block — customer aisles, not a service counter. The red 'Kitchen' dept name is printed on the shopping floor between five open-ended gondolas (x 937-992, y 239-356) stocked Appliances / Kitchen Gadgets / Canning; the PDF shows no counter or enclosure here. KITCHEN is a SERVICE_DEPTS substring, so the aisle corridors were condemned as a 1037-cell staff pocket; restoring them also suppresses the VERIFY the substring rule raises on the label.

Aisle 2 (Wine Accessories / Mixers) — a whole numbered aisle swallowed by the Deli disk's 12 pt bridge. The wine-bin scallops drawn on the east face of the Beer and Wine gondola pinch the corridor to ~11 pt at every arc, so the closing sealed its full length and left a 405-cell pocket between the free stubs at y<178 and y>278. The AISLE 2 badge at (746,336) sits at the foot of this same corridor.

Bakery customer frontage (east of the counter). The bakery island is walled on its west side by the Wine gondolas, so this ~13 pt strip between the counter rect (x 858-865) and the row of four-way display racks (x 878-890) is the ONLY floor a shopper can stand on to be served; the Bakery disk's bridge pinched it shut at each rack and culled 368 cells.

Open sales floor south of the Bakery (island displays). A 6.4 m x 2.4 m band of shopping floor carrying two four-way racks and a table between the bakery's south case line (y 480) and the front alley (y>504); the Bakery disk bridged the ~12 pt gaps around those islands and culled the whole band as a 201-cell pocket.
